gaps.sentence: We had to call ___ the order because the kitchen had closed.
The plane will drop ___ the parcels at the next farm.
gaps.explanation: drop off = deliver somebody/something; also become less (sales dropped off).

gaps.sentence: They want to try ___ the new software before buying.
gaps.explanation: try out = test something to see if it works.

gaps.sentence: She put her ideas ___ clearly and confidently.
gaps.explanation: put across = communicate an idea successfully.

gaps.sentence: These old boots are completely worn ___.
gaps.explanation: wear out = become thin/unusable through use.

gaps.sentence: The evidence finally backed ___ his version of events.
gaps.explanation: back up = support with evidence (a claim backs up a story).

gaps.sentence: The team was let ___ by its own supporters.
gaps.explanation: let somebody down = disappoint them by failing to help.
